categories.main_business_segments: DAISYO CORPORATION operates five main business segments: Restaurant Business (primarily Japanese-style izakaya chains such as 'Shoya' and 'Daisyo Suisan'), Wholesale & Logistics (food material wholesaling and integrated logistics for company-owned and franchise/voluntary chain stores), Real Estate (leasing and management of properties and subleasing of restaurant locations), Franchise & Voluntary Chain (FC/VC) Business (support and royalty income from franchise and voluntary chain members), and Other Businesses (including bread manufacturing and sales, and sales of tableware and kitchen equipment).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company emphasizes handmade Japanese cuisine, strict food safety and hygiene management, and traceability of ingredients. It operates two in-house research institutes for food safety and quality control, and utilizes a central kitchen and logistics centers for efficient supply chain management. The company also employs digital tools for marketing and operational efficiency, such as web reservations and digital content distribution.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are general consumers visiting the company's restaurant chains, as well as franchise and voluntary chain operators. The wholesale and logistics segment also serves other restaurants and external business clients. There are no single customers accounting for over 10% of sales, indicating a diversified customer base.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations are concentrated in Japan, with the majority of sales and assets located domestically. The company has a nationwide presence, with a particular focus on the Kanto region, but also operates stores and logistics centers across other major metropolitan areas in Japan.
categories.supply_chain_position: DAISYO operates primarily at the downstream (restaurant/retail) level, but also maintains significant midstream activities through its wholesale and logistics segment, supplying both its own stores and external clients with food materials and logistics services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening core restaurant brands through store renovations and new concepts, expanding the wholesale/logistics business, enhancing the FC/VC system, and driving operational efficiency via digital transformation (DX). The company is also focused on sustainability themes such as food safety, food loss reduction, sustainable sourcing, and human capital development. There is no significant proprietary R&D activity reported.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated from direct restaurant sales to consumers, wholesale of food materials, logistics services, property leasing, and franchise/royalty fees from FC/VC members. Additional revenue streams include the sale of bread and kitchenware.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: DAISYO competes in the mature and highly competitive Japanese restaurant and izakaya sector, facing competition from other large restaurant chains and food service companies. The company positions itself as a leader in traditional Japanese dining with a focus on food safety, quality, and value, but does not claim a dominant market share.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending August 2025, consolidated net sales were 52.6 billion yen, with operating profit of 1.2 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 1.17 billion yen. The company has returned to stable profitability after previous losses, with moderate sales growth (3.9% YoY) and a solid balance sheet (total assets: 29.5 billion yen, equity ratio: 38.2%).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: DAISYO emphasizes handmade, high-quality Japanese cuisine, strict food safety and hygiene standards, and a welcoming, family-oriented service ethos. Its differentiation lies in its commitment to ingredient traceability, in-house food safety research, and the ability to offer fresh, seasonal dishes at reasonable prices. The company also highlights its contribution to Japanese food culture and community well-being.
